rv-be:sales:9.4.note: still visible in code: salesRepUserId exists only on CreditMemoResponseDTO/CreditMemoMapper (l.141,177,215); InvoiceMapper, ItemReturnMapper, ItemReceiveMapper still emit the manager-row id as salesRepId; ItemReceiveDomainService.applyLocationAndSalesRep (~l.232-235) builds a bare SalesGeographyManager reference with no existence check.
rv-be:sales:9.4.summary: The field salesRepId holds a user id on sales orders and demands but a sales-geography-manager row id on invoices, item returns, item receives and credit memos. A screen that copies salesRepId from an order into an item receive links the wrong manager or fails a foreign-key check, which the API reports as a misleading 409 'referenced by other data'. Commission views can then credit the wrong person.
steps: Create a sales order for a customer whose rep is user U (POST /api/sales/orders); read GET /api/sales/orders/{id}: salesRepId is U's user id.
Create and approve an invoice for it; read GET /api/sales/invoices/{id}: salesRepId is the manager-row id, there is no salesRepUserId.
POST /api/sales/item-receives with salesRepId = the order's salesRepId (user id) or a non-existent id.
rv-be:sales:9.4.expected: One meaning for salesRepId (or an explicit salesRepUserId on every document); a non-existent rep id refused with 400 'Sales representative not found'.
rv-be:sales:9.4.actual: Different ids under the same name; a wrong id gives a 409 'referenced by other data' or links the wrong manager.
rv-be:sales:9.4.verify: After fix: GET an invoice, item return and item receive and check salesRepUserId equals the order's rep user; POST /api/sales/item-receives with an unknown salesRepId must answer 400.

rv-be:sales:9.5.note: still visible in code: CustomerRefundMapper.toApplicationResponses (~l.123) still uses ret.getCurrency() (item return) instead of the credit memo currency; local 'ret' variable declared at l.114 only for that.
rv-be:sales:9.5.summary: The refund screen shows each credit memo that a refund applies to. The currency of that row is read from the linked item return, so for a standalone memo, or a return saved with a blank currency, the row has no currency although the memo has one. Amounts are not affected.
steps: Create a standalone credit memo (no item return) in BDT and approve it.
POST /api/sales/customer-refunds applying that memo.
GET /api/sales/customer-refunds/{id} and read applications[0].currency.
rv-be:sales:9.5.expected: applications[0].currency equals the credit memo currency (BDT).
rv-be:sales:9.5.actual: applications[0].currency is null for a standalone memo.
rv-be:sales:9.5.verify: Repeat the steps: applications[0].currency must be the memo currency; for a return-linked memo it must be unchanged.

sales:B11.note: code still shows the gap: JournalLines.build (accounting/posting/translator/JournalLines.java l.165, l.212) throws 'the document has no amounts to post' at posting time only; sales invoice, order and demand create do not refuse a zero price, a sub-cent line or a date with no fiscal period up front. No e2e covers it.
sales:B11.summary: Some sales documents are saved successfully but can never be posted to the ledger: an invoice with price 0, a line worth 0.008 (rounds to nothing), totals with 3 decimals (24.999 versus 25.00 in the ledger), or a document dated where no fiscal period exists. The posting then fails in the background and nothing on screen tells the clerk; the month-end check later blocks the month.
steps: POST /api/sales/invoices for a delivered order line with quantity 5 and unitPrice 0.00.
Or POST /api/sales/invoices with 0.001 x 8.00.
Or POST /api/sales/demands, orders, delivery-orders and invoices dated 2030-06-01 (no fiscal period).
GET /api/sales/postings?documentType=SALES_INVOICE&documentId={id}.
sales:B11.expected: Each request refused with 400 and a readable message (or amounts rounded to the paisa and posted).
sales:B11.actual: Document saved (201), posting status FAILED 'the document has no amounts to post' / 'a journal line must carry an amount' / 'no financial period covers 2030-06-01'.
sales:B11.where: backend sales document create paths (InvoiceDomainService.create, SalesOrderDomainService, SalesDemandDomainService); accounting JournalLines.build
sales:B11.verify: Repeat steps 1-3: expect 400 at creation, and no invoice row with a FAILED posting afterwards.

saleschain:P3-B5.summary: Warehouse bins can be marked quarantine, wastage, blocked from normal picking or excluded from sellable stock, but a sales delivery order can still pick from such a bin and the stock leaves. The settings are stored and shown yet never enforced by sales, so damaged or held stock can be sold.

POST /api/sales/delivery-orders with lines[].inventoryDetails[].locationId = that bin.
Read the stock balance of that bin.

saleschain:P3-B5.actual: Delivery accepted and stock leaves the bin.
saleschain:P3-B5.verify: POST step 2: expect 400 naming the bin; a normal bin still works.

saleschain:P3-B7.note: still visible: no cancel/void/reverse endpoint on InvoiceController, ReceiptController or SalesOrderController; FinancialLedgerService.recordInvoiceCancelled (sales/ledger/service l.49) has no caller. Also a product decision (see saleschain:C14).
saleschain:P3-B7.summary: A wrong sales invoice, order or receipt cannot be cancelled or voided: the only correction is return plus credit memo, and a wrong receipt cannot be corrected at all. The code already knows the event INVOICE_CANCELLED, but nothing triggers it, and commission lifting cannot exclude cancelled invoices.
steps: POST /api/sales/invoices/{id}/cancel (also /void, /reverse, DELETE /api/sales/invoices/{id}).
Same for /api/sales/receipts/{id} and /api/sales/orders/{id}.

saleschain:SC-4.note: still visible in code: ECustomerLedgerEventType has only INVOICE_CREATED, INVOICE_CANCELLED, PAYMENT_RECEIVED, DEPOSIT_CREATED, DEPOSIT_APPLIED (sales/ledger/model/enums); no credit memo or refund event.
saleschain:SC-4.summary: The customer sub-ledger table (customer_ledger_entry) never records credit memos or refunds, so it shows the full invoice while the general ledger receivable (1130) is lower. Receivable figures read from that table, such as the month-closing receivable check, overstate what customers owe by every credit memo and refund.
steps: Invoice a customer, return goods, approve a credit memo (POST /api/sales/credit-memos then approve).
Compare the customer's ledger table balance (customer ledger / aging) with the GL account 1130 receivable.
saleschain:SC-4.expected: Credit memos and refunds appear in the customer ledger so it equals GL 1130.
saleschain:SC-4.actual: Table keeps the full invoice amount; e.g. 781.20 in the table against 677.04 in the GL.
saleschain:SC-4.verify: After the fix: the same scenario gives equal totals; the period-close 'Sales and Receivables' check shows difference 0.

saleschain:SC-5.note: still visible in code: JournalLines.build throws 'the document has no amounts to post' (l.165/l.212) for a document whose lines carry no money, and nothing in the sales invoice path skips a free-units-only invoice. No e2e covers it.

rv-be:sales:2.16.note: still visible in code: SalesTax.toFraction treats rate > 1 as a percent and rate <= 1 as a fraction (comment says so), so a rate of 1 means 100% and 0.8 means 80%; vatPart divides by (vatRate + aitRate) with no zero guard (~l.105).
rv-be:sales:2.16.summary: A tax rate is guessed from its size: anything above 1 is divided by 100, anything at or below 1 is used as is. A 1 percent or 0.8 percent AIT rate sent as 1 or 0.8 is read as 100% or 80%. vatPart also divides by zero if both configured rates are 0.

rv-be:sales:2.16.actual: Rate scale is guessed; zero combined rate breaks.
rv-be:sales:2.16.verify: Unit tests: toFraction(0.158)=0.158; vatPart with both rates 0 returns the whole tax amount without exception.

GET the customer summary (customer summary endpoint under /api/sales/customers/{id}).

rv-be:sales:9.8.note: still visible in code: SalesDemandMapper l.181 writes originalTaxAmount from withOriginals.get("vatAmount"), while SalesDemandCoordinationService stores VAT under ATTR_VAT = "vat" (l.64) and the UI sends "VatAmount".
rv-be:sales:9.8.summary: Each demand line is meant to keep the original VAT before pack sizing, but it reads a key nobody writes, so originalTaxAmount is always empty. Nothing reads it yet, so the before/after VAT comparison cannot be built.

GET the demand; read lines[].attributes.originalTaxAmount.

rv-be:sales:9.9.expected: Chosen rule (round up or decimal count).

saleschain:P3-B9.verify: Check each of the six calls separately; the first should return 400 at create.

sales:N1.note: decision still open; behaviour not changed in code that I could see: a receipt larger than the applications still posts Cr 1130 for the whole amount. No e2e asserts the advance ledger 2151.
sales:N1.summary: When a customer pays more than the invoices it is applied to, the unapplied part stays as a credit on the receivable account 1130 instead of moving to the customer-advance account 2151 that deposits use. Financial reports then show advances in two places.
steps: Create an invoice of 40, POST /api/sales/receipts with paymentAmount 100 applied 40.
GET /api/sales/postings?documentType=SALES_RECEIPT&documentId={id}.
sales:N1.expected: Owner decides: unapplied 60 goes to 2151 (advance) or stays on 1130.
sales:N1.where: backend sales receipt posting (SalesPostings.receipt / accounting translator)
sales:N1.verify: After the decision, the posting of the receipt shows the agreed split.

sales:N2.note: decision open: InvoiceController.apply-deposit (l.104) takes lines of depositId/invoiceId/amount, no date, so the application is dated the day of the call.
sales:N2.summary: Applying a customer deposit to an invoice has no date field, so the journal is dated the day of the call: an old invoice settled today posts in the current period, and in a closed period it is refused. Commission lifting also counts it in the call month.
steps: POST /api/sales/invoices/apply-deposit {lines:[{depositId,invoiceId,amount}]} for a December invoice in October of the next year.
Read the posting date.
sales:N2.expected: A date (or the later of deposit/invoice date) selectable and validated against open periods.
sales:N2.verify: After a decision: the application journal carries the chosen date.

sales:N3.note: decision open: InvoiceDomainService caps invoiced quantity by the ordered quantity (l.393-396), not by the delivered quantity, so an invoice before delivery is still accepted. No e2e asserts a refusal.
sales:N3.summary: An invoice can bill goods that have not been delivered: receivable and VAT are posted before the goods leave. It matches the invoice form (Delivery qty + Due qty) but the owner must confirm it is intended. It also lets an unshipped order count as commission lifting once paid.
steps: Approve a sales order with no delivery order.
POST /api/sales/invoices for the whole order.
sales:N3.expected: Owner decides: limit to delivered quantity or allow advance billing.
sales:N3.verify: After a decision to limit: step 2 returns 400.

sales:N4.note: decision open; invoice and ledger tax figures not changed in the code reviewed.
sales:N4.summary: The invoice shows tax as 15.8/115.8 of the gross (VAT plus AIT share) while the ledger posts Output VAT at 15/115.8, so the printed 'Tax' differs from the VAT ledger by the AIT share (8.5959 against 8.16 on a 63.00 invoice).
steps: Create an invoice of 63.00 gross for a corporate customer (15.8% in price).
Compare invoice taxAmount with the Output VAT line in GET /api/sales/postings.
sales:N4.expected: Owner decides which figure the invoice should show, or the AIT share is shown separately.
sales:N4.verify: After a decision: invoice tax equals ledger VAT, AIT shown on its own line.

sales:N5.note: decision open: rounding per invoice follows from per-document VAT; no change seen.
sales:N5.summary: If one order is invoiced in two parts, VAT is rounded on each invoice separately, so the two VATs can differ from the VAT of the whole order by one paisa (4.66 + 6.99 = 11.65 against 11.66).
steps: Invoice an order in two partial invoices.
Compare the sum of VAT with a single invoice of the whole order.
sales:N5.expected: Owner accepts the one-paisa drift or asks for allocation of the whole-order VAT.
sales:N5.verify: After a decision: partial VATs add up to the whole order's VAT.

sales:N7.note: decision open: ship checks the period (DeliveryOrderFulfillmentService l.1037-1038 postingPeriodGuard.requireOpen) but order, delivery draft and credit memo draft creation do not.
sales:N7.summary: Orders, delivery drafts and credit memo drafts dated in a closed month are accepted and refused only at ship or approval, so the clerk learns late. The refusal text itself is clear.
steps: Close a month.
POST /api/sales/orders dated in that month; then ship it.
sales:N7.expected: Owner decides: refuse at creation or keep the late check.
sales:N7.actual: Accepted at create, refused at ship.
sales:N7.verify: After a decision to refuse early: step 2 create returns 409 naming the closed period.

saleschain:C15.note: decision open: item return takes quantity in sales units; no unit field.
saleschain:C15.summary: A return can only be typed in the item's sales unit; there is no pack-size conversion, so a customer returning 2 cartons must be typed as the unit count. The note recommends offering the pack list on the return screen.

Look for a unit or pack selector.

saleschain:C15.where: backend ItemReturnRequestDTO; frontend item return form
saleschain:C15.verify: After a decision: returning 2 cartons stores the converted unit quantity.

saleschain:C3.note: decision open: delivery order create does not compare the warehouse of the picked bin with the order's warehouse (no such check found in DeliveryOrderFulfillmentService).
saleschain:C3.summary: A delivery order may pick stock from a bin in another warehouse than the order's warehouse, silently. Stock can leave the wrong place without anyone noticing.
steps: POST /api/sales/delivery-orders for an order of warehouse A with inventoryDetails.locationId in a bin of warehouse B.
saleschain:C3.expected: Owner decides: refuse, or show as a warehouse change.
saleschain:C3.verify: After a decision to refuse: the request returns 400.

saleschain:C7.note: decision open: no creator-not-approver rule found in the workflow code (grep for self-approval returned nothing).
saleschain:C7.summary: May the person who created a document also approve it, if their role is the named approver? Today yes. The note recommends no by default, as a setting, for segregation of duties.
steps: Give one user the maker and approver role, create a demand, then POST /api/workflow/tasks/{taskId}/complete as the same user.
saleschain:C7.expected: Owner decides; if no, approval by the creator returns 403/409.
saleschain:C7.where: backend workflow task completion (platform workflow module)
saleschain:C7.verify: After a decision: step 1 as the creator is refused.

saleschain:C8.note: decision open: no price-override permission found in sales demand/order create.
saleschain:C8.summary: Who may sell below list price or give a manual discount? Today anyone with demand create can enter a price of 1.00 or 0.00 against a list price of 8.00, and there is no override permission or approval rule on unit price.

saleschain:C8.expected: Owner decides: new permission or approval rule on unit price.
saleschain:C8.verify: After a decision: below-list price needs the permission or an approval.
